newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian-U.S. crew undock from Mir for brief trip.
newsitem.headline: Russian-U.S. crew undock from Mir for brief trip.

text.p: Two Russian cosmonauts and a NASA astronaut undocked from the Mir space station in their Soyuz escape capsule on Friday for a 45-minute ride in which they will film the station, Mission Control said.
Commander Anatoly Solovyov, engineer Pavel Vinogradov and British-born NASA physicist Michael Foale were due to redock with Mir at 6.10 p.m. Moscow time (1410 GMT).
"We've undocked," Solovyov was heard telling Korolyov Mission Control, outside Moscow, by radio.
Film footage from the Soyuz, fed directly to Mission Control, showed the craft moving slowly away from Mir.
The new crew is preparing for risky repairs to fix damage done when Mir collided with its cargo ship while it was redocking on June 25. The accident was the worst mishap in Mir's 11 years in orbit.

The crew enjoyed a change of luck on Thursday when they repaired the main Elektron oxygen generating system just as the old crew shut the hatch on their Soyuz capsule to return to earth, officials said.

Previous commander Vasily Tsibliyev and flight engineer Alexander Lazutkin returned safely to earth on Thursday after enduring one of the most gruelling six months in the history of human space flight.
They were undergoing rehabilitation and readjustment to life with gravity on Friday at the Star City cosmonaut training centre outside Moscow, officials said.
They landed in the steppes of Kazakhstan and celebrated with caviar and red wine before greeting their families at Star City and taking their first baths in half a year.
Flight officials were relieved that the oxygen system was repaired disposing of fears that they might have to wait for the U.S. shuttle to bring new parts in late September.
But the prospect of the undocking and redocking caused a few jitters at Mission Control.
"An undocking is a pretty tense event," said Yuri Antoshechkin, head of Mission Control's analysis team.
Deputy Flight Director Igor Goncharov told Reuters: "They will undock, go around the station to look at its construction and video it...They will dock at the other port near the Spektr module."

The Spektr module was punctured during the June accident, and is now sealed off from the rest of the station. The two Russian cosmonauts will open the hatch next Wednesday to reattach cables linked to Spektr's solar panels in a risky repair job intended to restore the ship's energy system.
Redocking the Soyuz near Spektr will allow a quick escape if repairs go wrong.

To prepare for the Friday Soyuz trip, the crew shut off the oxygen system they had worked so hard to repair. "We turned it on yesterday evening and it worked fine until this morning, and we have turned it off for two reasons," Antoshechkin said.

"One, to lower energy demands on the station during the undocking today," he said. "And second, because it can only be turned off by the crew, and in case that, knock on wood, the undocking fails, then we couldn't turn it off later."
All three crew members were packed into the Soyuz for Friday's flight because space officials do not want to leave anyone on Mir without an emergency escape vehicle.
On Sunday, Mir will redock with its old Progress resupply ship, the very procedure that caused the June accident. This time however the crew expects to do the operation on automatic pilot.
